 In The High Court At Calcutta

 Mousumi Mukherjee & Ors

-VS-  ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd. & Anr.
 Mr. Sk. Abu Abbas Uddin,
 Ms. Nahid Rahaman  ... for the appellants-claimants  Mr. Parimal Kumar Pahari  ... for the respondent no.1- insurance company This appeal is preferred against the judgment and award dated 19th September, 2019 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Fast Track, 1st Court, Sealdah, 24 Parganas (South) in MAC case no. 02 of 2016 granting compensation of Rs.3,43,600/- together with interest in favour of the claimants under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Immediately, he was shifted to NRS Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata where the attending doctor declared him brought dead.

which have been marked as Exhibits 1 to 18 respectively.

by the self-same order, his attainment of majority has been directed to be recorded in the memorandum of appeal.

Upon considering the materials on record and evidence adduced on behalf of the claimants, the learned Tribunal granted compensation of Rs.3,43,600/- together with interest in favour of the claimants under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award of the learned Tribunal,
the claimants have preferred the present appeal.

Mr. Abu Abbas Uddin, learned advocate for the appellants-claimants, submits that the learned Tribunal erred in determining the income of the victim despite the fact that the salary certificate and the certificate relating to his part-time job have been proved in support of monthly income of the deceased.

He further submits that the claimants are entitled to an amount equivalent to 25% of the annual income of the deceased towards future prospect and general damages of Rs. 70,000/- under the conventional heads.

Further more, since at the time of accident, the victim was 48 years of age,
the multiplier should be 13 instead of 11.
Moreover, the number of dependants at the time of accident being four, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be 1/4th instead of 1/3rd.
In the light of the aforesaid submissions, he prays for enhancement of the compensation amount.

In reply to the contentions raised on behalf of the appellants-claimants, Mr. Parimal Kumar Pahari,
learned advocate for the respondent no. 1 insurance company submits that the salary certificate shows that the victim was an employee under "Banik Rubber Industries (India) Pvt. Ltd."
whereas such document has been produced by an officer of "Ajanta Shoes (India) Pvt. Ltd." and as such is not acceptable.

He further submits that no master roll relating to the employment of the victim in "Banik Rubber Industries (India) Pvt. Ltd." has been produced to primarily establish the employment of the victim in the said concern.

So far as the part-time job is concerned, no document has been produced showing disbursement of salary from the organization namely, "H. K. Das & Co."
in favour of the victim.
He fairly submits that since the accident has taken place in the year 2016, at best the income of the victim can be considered at Rs. 5,000/- per month.

With regard to future prospect, multiplier, general damages and deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased are concerned, he submits that those aspects should be determined on the basis of the propositions laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Sethi and Others reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 and Sarla Verma and others versus Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009 ACJ 1298.

sentences.text: Having heard the learned advocates for the respective parties, following issues have fallen for consideration.

Firstly, whether the learned Tribunal erred in determining the income of the deceased; secondly, whether the claimants are entitled to an amount equivalent to 25% of the annual income of the deceased towards future prospect; thirdly, whether the multiplier should be 13 instead of 11 adopted by the learned Tribunal; fourthly, whether the claimants are entitled to general damages of Rs. 70,000/- under the conventional heads; and lastly, whether the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be 1/4th instead of 1/3rd adopted by the Mousumi Mukherjee & Ors vs Icici Lombard General Insurance Co. ... on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54536947/

sentences.text: 2 learned Tribunal.
With regard to the determination of the income of the deceased it is found that the learned Tribunal has determined the income of the deceased at Rs.3,000/- per month.

The claimants in order to establish the income of the deceased victim examined one Satya Kumar Mishra as P.W.4 employee of "Ajanta Shoes (India) Pvt. Ltd." who produced the Salary Certificate marked as Exhibit-15, E.S.I.
Certificate marked as Exhibit-16, Trade License marked Exhibit-17, Registration Certificate marked Exhibit-18 and Pan Card of the Company as Exhibit-19 and one Suvendu Das as P.W.3, one of the partners "H. K. Das & Co." who produced appointment letter marked Exhibit-12, Salary Certificate marked as Exhibit-13.
P.W. 4 in his evidence-in-chief deposed that the victim was an employee in their concern.

On going through the Employees' State Insurance Corporation Temporary Identity Certificate Exhibit-16, it is found that the deceased was employed with "Banik Rubber Industries (India) Pvt.
Ltd." and his date of appointment is 1st of April, 2012.

Certificate of incorporation pursuant to change of name dated 25th April, 2018 (Exhibit-18) shows that the name of "Banik Rubber Industries (India) Pvt. Ltd." has been changed to "Ajanta Shoes (India) Pvt. Ltd."

From the aforesaid evidence it is found that the claimants could establish that the victim was an employee of "Banik Rubber Industries (India) Pvt. Ltd." whose name was subsequently changed to "Ajanta Shoes (India) Pvt. Ltd."
P.W.4 being officer of H.R. Department of "Ajanta Shoes (India) Pvt. Ltd." proved the salary certificate of the victim marked as Exhibit-15.
It is found that such salary certificate is bereft of the month for which the same has been issued.
The certificate also does not mention the date of its issuance.
In cross examination.
P.W.-4 has stated that it would not be possible for him to produce the salary register of "Banik Rubber Industries (India) Pvt. Ltd.".
Thus though the employment of the deceased with "Banik Rubber Industries (India) Pvt. Ltd." has been proved but the salary has not been established.

So far as the part time employment with "H. K. Das & Co." is concerned, it is found that P.W.3 who produced salary certificate (Exhibit-13) deposed that he has not produced any document showing that the victim used to receive salary from their organization and has also not brought the register showing that the victim was an employee of their concern.
Such being the position the part time employment of the victim has also not been established.

However, bearing in mind that the victim was working in a concern and also keeping in mind the economic factors and cost of essential commodities prevailing in the year 2016 the income of the victim is considered at Rs.6,000/- per month.

With regard to the issue relating to future prospect, since at the time of accident the victim was 48 years of age and was on fixed income, following observations of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (supra), the claimants are entitled to an amount of equivalent to 25% of the annual amount of the deceased towards future prospect.
So far as the multiplier is concerned, it is found that the learned Tribunal has adopted multiplier of 11.

However, since the victim was 48 years of age at the time of accident, hence following the observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (supra) the multiplier should be 13 instead of 11 adopted by the learned Tribunal.

sentences.text:
Further the claimants are also entitled to general damages under the conventional heads of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses to the tune of Rs. 15,000/-, Rs. 40,000/- and Rs.
15,000/- respectively following Pranay Sethi (supra).

Coming to the last issue relating to deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased,
it is found that the Tribunal has deducted 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
However, it is found from the materials on record that at the time of accident the number of dependants of the deceased was 4.
Following the proposition in Sarla Verma (supra) the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be 1/4th instead of 1/3rd.
Other factors have not been challenged in this appeal.

Bearing in mind the above factors, calculation is made hereunder:
Calculation of Compensation Monthly Income Rs.6,000/-
 Annual Income Rs.72,000/-
 (Rs.6,000/- x 12)
 Add: 25% of the annual income Rs. 18,000/-
 towards future prospect  Rs. 90,000/-
 Deduction: 1/4th towards personal Rs. 22,500/-
 and living expenses  Rs. 67,500/-

Multiply 13 Rs.8,77,500/-
 (Rs. 67,500/-x 13)
 Add: General damage Rs.70,000/-
 Loss of estate: Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of consortium: Rs.40,000/-
Funeral expenses: Rs.15,000/-
Total amount Rs.9,47,500/-
Accordingly, the claimants are entitled to Rs.9,47,500/- together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till payment.

The Respondent No.1-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount of compensation together with interest by way of cheque before the learned Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta within a period of six weeks from date.

It is found from the affidavit and documents annexed thereto filed by the appellants-claimants that the Respondent No.1-Insurance Company has deposited four cheques before the learned Tribunal on 31.10.2019 which are still lying with the learned Tribunal.
Accordingly, the Respondent No.1-Insurance Company is granted liberty to withdraw the aforesaid cheques from the learned Tribunal.

sentences.text: Appellants-claimants are directed to deposit ad valorem Court fees on the compensation assessed, if not already paid.

Upon deposit of aforesaid amount of compensation and interest indicated above,
learned Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta shall release the amount in favour of appellants-claimants, after making payment of Rs. 40,000/- to appellant no.1, widow of the deceased towards spousal consortium, in equal proportion, on satisfaction of their identity and payment of ad valorem Court fees, if not already paid.

Appellant no.1, being the mother and natural guardian of minor appellant no.4, shall receive the share of the minor on his behalf and shall keep the same in a fixed deposit scheme of any nationalised bank or post office till attainment of majority of the said minor.
With the aforesaid observations, the appeal stands disposed of.
The impugned judgement and award is modified to the above extent.
No order as to costs.
All the connected applications, if any, stand disposed of.
Interim order, if any, stands vacated.
Urgent photostat copy of this order, if applied for, be given to the parties upon compliance of necessary legal formalities.

( Bivas Pattanayak, J.)
